providers.notes: Strongest at driving the dev loop as well. Historical strict-code-mode and direct-MCP receipts remain readable through src/blind/receipt_binding.ts.

Also a strong dev-loop driver. Ships a CLI, but blind-tester/run.sh has no launch branch for it and there is no reader for its session logs, so nothing here can PROVE what tools it saw: its sessions are hand-played and ingested, which is what operator_attested means. This becomes runner_enforced the day the runner can launch and audit it, and its earlier sessions keep their original, honest label.

Well suited to cheap mass-parallel volume cohorts. Ships a CLI, but blind-tester/run.sh has no launch branch for it and there is no reader for its session logs, so its sessions are hand-played and ingested as operator_attested until one exists.

A headless-capable Grok CLI DOES ship now (verified: grok 1.0.5 offers -p/--single, --output-format, --tools and an mcp subcommand), so the old 'no CLI exists' note was stale. This stays operator_attested and kind=desktop_client anyway, deliberately: `blind-tester/run.sh` can only PROVE blindness for codex, by reading Codex's own rollout logs, and flipping this to headless_cli would let a grok cohort past argument validation only to die inside the runner. Grok also takes its prompt as an argument rather than on STDIN, and has no --mcp-config flag, so it does not fit the launch contract either. Sessions are captured in the client and ingested with `npm run playtest:ingest`; revisit only when a rollout-log reader for this vendor exists.
